messages:
Ethan L.: Quick sync — we need a clear rule for compact compare presets ownership when a route is forked/duplicated. Current confusion: new route either inherits original owner (confusing) or becomes ownerless and system-owned (also bad). Thoughts?

Priya K.: My take: UX-wise people expect a copied route to start with the same look+filters but they also expect to be able to change ownership. So default to 'copied-by' as owner (the user who triggered the fork). Keep a link to the origin so teams can trace back.

Sam (Design): +1 to copied-by. Two quick design constraints: (1) show a small origin pill on the header like: "Copied from /payments/charge (team: Billing)" so users can quickly see provenance; (2) when copying across teams, prompt a modal "Assign to which team?" to avoid accidental cross-team sharing.

Xiao W.: Implementation note: our saved-query model currently has {"scope": "route|team|global", "owner_id": <user>, "team_id": <team>}. For copy-on-fork we can set owner_id = acting_user, team_id = new_route.team_id, and add origin_metadata: "origin_route_id" + "origin_saved_query_id". That last field needs to be optional string on the DB model. Perf-wise OK.

Jonah B.: Two gotchas: (a) telemetry attribution — we currently tag events by saved_query_id. If copied, we should either reset telemetry (new saved_query_id) OR retain a pointer to origin so historical metrics can be stitched. I vote for new saved_query_id + origin pointer so metrics are clean but joinable. (b) quotas — do we count copied queries against the destination team's quota? I think yes (they own it now).

Priya K.: For telemetry, stitching is important for migration analysis. UX needs both: show "Usage since copy" and optionally include "merged view with origin". Could be a toggle.

Ethan L.: Agreed on new id + origin pointer. For quotas, count against destination team. We should also enforce a soft limit and surface a CTA to request more slots if team hits quota while copying.

Sam (Design): About the merge view toggle — add a small dropdown in the compare header: "View: Current / Origin / Combined". Combined will overlay metrics from origin with faded colors. Keep it off by default because stale origin can mislead.

Xiao W.: API contract proposal (very small):
```json
POST /api/v1/saved_queries.copy
{
  "saved_query_id": "sq_123",
  "target_route_id": "route_456",
  "assign_team_id": "team_789"  // optional, default to target route team
}

Response 201:
{
  "saved_query_id": "sq_999",
  "origin_saved_query_id": "sq_123",
  "owner_id": "user_abc"
}
```
This follows copy semantics, leaves telemetry independent, and returns origin.

Jonah B.: Implementation flag: add a feature-flag for rollouts so we can test behavior across org types (multi-team orgs first). infra-bot: created feature flag "sq.copy_origin_metadata" on staging.

infra-bot: Feature flag "sq.copy_origin_metadata" created by infra-bot. Active: staging only.

Priya K.: One more thing — export/share links. If someone shares a deep link to the copied preset, we should redirect to the new saved_query_id. But if referring to the origin we should still resolve origin_saved_query_id -> new_id map if it exists to avoid 404s. Add canonical redirect logic.

Xiao W.: Noted. I'll add an id mapping table (small TTL cleanup) so we can redirect for up to 30 days post-copy. After that we fall back to origin metadata page.

Ethan L.: Action items: (1) Xiao: implement DB origin_metadata + API change, add redirect mapping TTL 30d; (2) Jonah: quota counting + soft-limit CTA; (3) Sam/Priya: mockups for origin pill + compare dropdown (due EOD Wed); (4) Product: flagged rollout gating for multi-team orgs. If anyone objects to the approach call it out now, otherwise I'll put a PR checklist.

Jonah B.: No objections. Will add quota unit tests.

Sam (Design): Will post mocks in #design-review.

Priya K.: I'll draft the rollout plan and copy for the modal.

Ethan L.: Cool — thanks all.
